text:
ana_cs: FYI customer ACME reports a quality regression after yesterday's rollout. Previously extracted invoice line items cleanly, now returns unrelated tokens. They say behavior changed after the deploy.

mike_ml: Can you paste the exact customer prompt + the response they observed? Our internal eval on the latest model passed.

ana_cs: here's the redacted snippet from the customer (they confirmed we can repro with redaction):
```json
{"user_message": "Extract line items from invoice:\n1. Widget A $12.00\n2. Service X $120.00", "metadata": {"source":"mobile_app","truncate": false}}
```
Observed response:
```
["Widget Q", "Payment due"]
```
Expected: ["Widget A", "Service X"]

mike_ml: Hmm — our eval harness uses canonical spacing and includes a system role 'You are a helpful assistant'. Do they include system messages or any client-side preprocessing? Also what decode params?

ana_cs: They call the chat/generate endpoint directly from mobile, no explicit system role, temperature 0.0, top_p 1.0, model: redwood-open-7b-quant (default variant). No extra postprocessing on their side.

lin_runtime: Deploy logs show release v2.14 rolled out last night at 1838999000; canary -> stable overnight. Any noted config changes?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: release v2.14 (model routing + small decoding fallback) deployed 1838999000, canary 10% -> stable. Changelog note: "default_sampling: fallback_to_top_p" added to decoding path.

jordan_pm: That sampling fallback could change decode for short multi-line inputs. Our internal eval sets might not cover mobile_app formatting. Mike — could kernel/fallback interaction + quantization be the source?

mike_ml: Possible. The fallback path triggers when primary decoder kernel returns marginally low logprobs for punctuation-heavy prefixes. Our eval suite didn't include invoice-like multiline items with trailing newline. Can we reproduce with the exact HTTP payload? Ana, can you paste headers + body?

ana_cs: Redacted curl from customer (they sent the raw request):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-7b-quant","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Extract line items from invoice:\n1. Widget A $12.00\n2. Service X $120.00"}],"temperature":0.0}'
```

mike_ml: Running that locally against the deployed artifact with the fallback enabled... result matches the customer's bad output. Running same payload against an environment with fallback disabled returns correct extraction. So regression tied to the new "fallback_to_top_p" decoding path interacting with quantized kernel.

lin_runtime: Proposed mitigation: revert the default_sampling config change for the quantized 7b variant (hotfix) or force that model to skip the fallback path while we investigate. I can push config and gate rollout.

jordan_pm: Do we want a full rollback or a targeted hotfix? Rolling back entire v2.14 might be heavier; hotfix to revert sampling default for that model seems fine if it's low-risk. CS: inform the customer and offer model pin to older variant as a short-term workaround.

ana_cs: Customer prefers platform fix (they don't want to change code). They're waiting on a patch.

lin_runtime: Pushing hotfix now to revert sampling default for redwood-open-7b-quant. I'll push config and do a small canary.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: hotfix release v2.14.1 — revert "default_sampling: fallback_to_top_p" for redwood-open-7b-quant. Deployed at 1839001300, canary 5%.

mike_ml: Re-ran the customer's exact curl against the hotfixed routing — now the output matches expected extraction.

jordan_pm: Action items: 1) CS to confirm with customer and close escalation if fixed. 2) Eng to add the customer's prompt (redacted) to the regression test harness and create a deterministic test covering trailing newlines + mobile metadata. 3) Research to root-cause the quantized kernel + fallback interaction and produce mitigation / kernel fix. 4) Postmortem + release notes documenting the change and quick rollback guidance.

ana_cs: I'll relay to ACME and ask them to re-run their workload now. I'll update here when they confirm. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

mike_ml: I'll file a PR with the regression test and assign to applied-ml for investigation.

lin_runtime: I'll schedule a follow-up runbook to avoid silent decoding-path changes without regression coverage.

ana_cs: ACME confirmed — behavior restored, they see correct extractions. Marking this resolved on the customer side; still need the postmortem and test coverage.

jordan_pm: Thanks team. We'll capture learnings and tighten pre-rollout eval matrices.

ana_cs: closing loop with ACME now. Cheers.
